Thanks for the summary, Sergio — good triage. I reviewed the draft and made edits in Peridot_OrderForm_Redline_Kimberly.pdf. High-level guidance below:

1) Net terms
- We should avoid Net 60 as a default for new mid-market customers. If we can get a PO and a signed order form, Finance can support Net 45 for the first 3 months, converting to Net 30 after the initial qualification period. This is a programmable exception — we'll document it as a one-time concession tied to PO issuance.

2) Tax withholding (critical)
- Redwood's policy: customer is responsible for any withholding tax unless Redwood expressly agrees to gross-up. We're open to a gross-up arrangement but only if Peridot accepts the gross-up amount (i.e., Redwood invoices grossed-up amounts) OR provides legally binding proof that the withholding will be credited back to Redwood.
- Alternative: accept withholding if Peridot provides a withholding certificate and agrees to a withhold-and-provide-evidence workflow; then Redwood will issue a credit upon receipt of official receipts. This is operationally heavier and will require invoicing team sign-off.

3) Invoice header & PO
- Acceptable. We should request that PO reference the order form and attach the signed order form to the PO. Finance will want the VAT ID and the remit-to entity clearly listed.

4) Contract language
- Markus: please confirm the redline on Section 6 (Payment; Taxes) and add an explicit path for evidence submission (with timelines). Also add an escape hatch: if cumulative withheld taxes exceed X% in a rolling 90-day window, Redwood can pause service pending resolution.

Karthik — can you confirm if Revenue Ops can process a Net 45 pilot and what controls you'd want to mitigate credit risk? If Net 60 is insisted on, what collection instruments would you need (advance payment, irrevocable PO, letter of credit)?

If everyone agrees, I'll take the redline to Marta and propose a short call Monday to finalize.

Kimberly
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the detail — quick operational answers from Finance/Revenue Ops: 

- Net 45 pilot: acceptable for first two billing cycles provided we have a valid PO that references the signed order form and an approved billing contact. We need the PO to include a clause committing to timely dispute handling (30 days SLA).
- Net 60: not acceptable as a standard. If Peridot insists, we need one of the following before we accept: (a) 25% advance payment at signature, or (b) an irrevocable bank guarantee / LC covering first 3 months, or (c) an explicit gross-up agreement where Redwood invoices grossed-up amounts and Peridot supplies withholding receipts.
- Withholding processing: we can process withhold-and-credit but require Peridot to submit official tax receipts within 60 days of withholding. We will issue a credit only upon receipt of official documentation. We will not absorb withholding without a gross-up.
- Operational ask: please instruct Peridot to include billing contact + remit-to entity in the PO. Also ask them to use the exact VAT ID they provided.

Action items:
- Kimberly/Markus: finalize the proposed Payment & Taxes language (escape hatch + evidence workflow).
- Sergio: propose Net 45 pilot with above caveats to Peridot and offer a call Monday 09/21 to close.
- I'll prep Finance's PO checklist and a short note on acceptable collection instruments.

Karthik
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
